construction_notes.text: From the state Housing Element Annual Progress Report, through 2025.
505 market-rate apartments, 132 affordable apartments, 100 townhomes. Application cites SB 330 and density bonus.

CTCAC application CA-26-739, 211 River Oaks Parkway: 132 total units, 130 low-income. Application, not an award: bond request $23,243,271, federal credit request $3,985,466 (CDLAC September 8, 2026 applicant list). The record's 737-unit count is a different figure; kept as is.

Valley Oak Partners was named project developer in October 2025. A February 2026 article reports TPG and Angelo Gordon bought the site through an affiliate and calls this a pivot from the previous development under Valley Oak Partners. Who carries the project forward is not stated.

City of San Jose permit H23-041 (Site Development Permit/Amendment, folder year 2023), status Approved, issue date 2025-10-29: "Site Development Permit to allow the construction of a multi-phased, 737-unit multifamily residential development on an approximately 9.82-gross acre site consisting of: -Market Rate Phase: A seven-story, 505-unit market-rate apartment building -Affordab" (city text cut off at 255 characters)
City of San Jose permit PRE23-111 (Prelim - Focused (Policy Review, No Plans), folder year 2023), status Complete: "SB330 preliminary application for 737 units"

Draft EIR filing: 100 market-rate townhomes and two apartment buildings with 637 units, 737 total, 76.2 units per acre; one apartment building holds 130 affordable units plus two market-rate manager units. Vesting Tentative Map to subdivide two lots into 31 lots.

San Jose Spotlight (November 2024) reports 132 affordable apartments, 20% of the apartments, including building managers; three-story townhomes, five-story affordable building and seven-story market-rate building.

City permit T23-028 (Approved): Vesting Tentative Map for 31 lots (16 residential, 5 private street, 10 open space) and up to 100 residential condominium units. AD26-430 (Under Review, filed 2026-06-23 by Risewell Homes) changes the townhome phase: removes fourth-floor roof decks and changes the clubhouse and pool equipment room.
Water Supply Assessment memo: maximum project demand about 99 acre-feet per year; memo refers to expected 2030 completion.
